record.paper_title: A review of results and open problems on mathematical models of motion of viscoelastic media of Jeffreys' type
record.original_question: Can one construct any generalized solution of the stationary boundary-value problem for the Jeffreys-type system (0.2), (0.4), (0.5), (2.18) without imposing restrictions on the coefficients, the external force, or the initial data?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an incompressible viscoelastic fluid of Jeffreys type occupying a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2,3$) with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$. The motion is governed by the stationary system

$$\rho(v\cdot\nabla)v - \mathrm{Div}\,\sigma = \rho f, \qquad \mathrm{div}\,v=0\quad\text{in }\Omega,$$

with the Jeffreys constitutive law for the deviatoric stress $\sigma$,

$$\sigma + \lambda_1 \big((v\cdot\nabla)\sigma + \sigma W(v) - W(v)\sigma\big) = 2\eta\Big(\mathcal E(v) + \lambda_2\big((v\cdot\nabla)\mathcal E(v) + \mathcal E(v)W(v) - W(v)\mathcal E(v)\big)\Big),$$

where $\mathcal E(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v + \nabla v^\top)$ is the rate-of-strain tensor, $W(v)=\tfrac12(\nabla v - \nabla v^\top)$ is the vorticity tensor, $\rho>0$ is the density, $\eta>0$ is the viscosity, and $0<\lambda_2<\lambda_1$ are the relaxation and retardation times. The system is closed with the no-slip boundary condition $v\big|_{\partial\Omega}=0$ together with appropriate boundary conditions for $\sigma$ on the inflow part of $\partial\Omega$, and a prescribed external body force $f$.

Question: Does there exist a generalized (weak) solution $(v,\sigma)$ of this stationary boundary-value problem for arbitrary admissible coefficients $\rho,\eta,\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ and arbitrary external force $f$, without imposing any smallness, regularity, or other restrictive conditions on the coefficients or the data?
artifact.status_search_result: Existence of weak solutions for the stationary boundary-value problem of the Jeffreys-type viscoelastic system has been established in several settings (e.g., inhomogeneous Dirichlet conditions via elliptic regularization and topological degree, and flow-through problems in bounded domains without smallness assumptions on forcing/boundary data). However, these constructions typically rely on specific regularizations (such as replacing the vorticity tensor by a spatial average in Jeffreys' law) or particular boundary configurations, so a fully unrestricted construction for the original (non-regularized) Jeffreys system with arbitrary coefficients and data is not yet available in full generality.

status_evidence.title: An inhomogeneous boundary value problem for the stationary motion equations of Jeffreys viscoelastic medium
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of weak solutions of an inhomogeneous boundary value problem for the stationary motion equations of Jeffreys viscoelastic medium is proven; the weak solution set is shown to be sequentially weakly closed.
status_evidence.claim: Weak solvability of the stationary Jeffreys boundary-value problem has been proved in inhomogeneous settings.

status_evidence.title: Flow-through problem for a Jeffreys type viscoelastic fluid
status_evidence.snippet: Steady-state flow of an incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid through a bounded domain; weak solutions constructed via vanishing artificial viscosity and Leray–Schauder degree without smallness assumptions on forcing and boundary data.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results construct stationary weak solutions without smallness conditions, but using regularization techniques.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of weak solutions for the initial-boundary value problem in the Jeffreys model
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of weak solutions to the initial-boundary value problem of the Jeffreys model of motion of a viscoelastic medium.
status_evidence.claim: Related evolutionary problem admits weak solutions, supporting partial progress on the broader program.
